cases.expected_relation: Identical visible image should have no style or source-fidelity discrepancy when all roles intentionally use the same immutable image.
evidence: The three inspected role images are byte-identical, so the specified visible features and content are identical.

cases.expected_relation: Identical visible source image should have no discrepancy in the self-match calibration, demonstrating source-content comparison is not person-only.
evidence: The three inspected role images are byte-identical; observed subject content, garment marking, composition, and technical state match exactly.

cases.expected_relation: The unstyled photographic source preserves content but is a strong reusable-style mismatch against the illustrated poster truth.
evidence: Candidate is a photographic image rather than opaque editorial-anime cel-shaded poster print.
It lacks the limited print palette, navy ink contour, paper/overprint behavior, and abstract support hierarchy.
It visibly preserves the source content because it is the source image itself.

cases.expected_relation: The same cross-domain mismatch remains high regardless of visual presentation order after role labels are retained.
evidence: Visible differences are medium-level and remain unchanged when presentation order changes; labels, not order, define roles.

pass_criteria: Both self-matches have zero discrepancy; cross-domain mismatch has style losses greater than 0.75 with source_fidelity at or below 0.05; order-swap component deltas are zero.
summary: All four observable calibration relations passed. This provisional suite is evidence for a stable v3 rubric and must be retained unchanged during this iteration.
